requirements.statement: Every task at or after XT-083 binds approved requirement criteria to a task-type-appropriate test contract before implementation begins, without rewriting accepted or already-planned task provenance.
acceptance_criteria: CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-CONTRACT-001: every governed criterion has a stable ID, observable statement, explicit negative definition, implementation owner, acceptance owner, and required evidence contract.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-CONTRACT-002: every governed task declares one proof mode appropriate to feature, bugfix, refactor, test, governance, investigation, or acceptance work before claim.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-CONTRACT-003: plan approval binds criterion semantics, task mappings, negative definitions, and evidence contracts in the canonical approval digest.
Negative: a prose checkbox, coverage percentage, generic repository gate, or task completion state without criterion-level evidence does not satisfy the contract.
Negative: tasks before XT-083, accepted task records, and tasks already registered by this bootstrap plan are not retroactively rewritten or assigned fabricated TDD history.

requirements.statement: The harness mechanically proves that governed behavior tests existed and produced the expected result before the implementation that satisfies them.
acceptance_criteria: CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-PROOF-001: a trusted checkpoint proves the focused gate passes at task base, fails for the attributed Red test revision, and passes at reviewed head.

CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-PROOF-002: the complete base-to-Red commit history touches only declared test, fixture, scenario, test-registration, and task-record paths; adding and later reverting production code still fails.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-PROOF-003: the harness freezes the gate command, criterion mapping, failure fingerprint, and proof-surface digest, and rejects deletion or weakening after Red.

CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-PROOF-004: feature and governance tasks use Red-Green proof, bugfixes retain regression proof, refactors use characterization equivalence, test infrastructure proves a sentinel or mutant, and investigations cannot close product criteria.
Negative: compilation-tool absence, command-not-found, timeout, crash, skipped test, unrelated assertion, or an unregistered command is not valid Red evidence.
Negative: production changes committed before the Red checkpoint, mutable test oracles, and tests added only after implementation fail review.

requirements.statement: Acceptance closes a criterion only with structured evidence from the exact integrated candidate and every required scenario, platform, role, job, and artifact.
acceptance_criteria: CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-EVIDENCE-001: evidence records criterion ID, scenario IDs, source SHA, packaged binary digests, gate and workflow digests, platform and role matrix, result, run URL, and artifact digest.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-EVIDENCE-002: acceptance reruns required gates against the exact integrated candidate instead of trusting that an upstream test task once reached done.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-EVIDENCE-003: required remote jobs, matrices, artifacts, and no-skip policy are validated before criterion closure and branch publication.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-EVIDENCE-004: unit, integration, contract snapshot, smoke, E2E, security, reliability, and performance evidence remain distinct and are selected by declared risk.

Negative: fake gateways, in-memory transports, one process, unauthenticated sockets, stale artifacts, partial matrices, skipped jobs, and generic make verify results cannot satisfy an E2E or specialized criterion.

requirements.statement: Future task generation, prompts, stale-base checks, review, integration, and acceptance enforce the TDD contract while existing accepted and in-flight work remains valid.
acceptance_criteria: CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-ADOPTION-001: new task generation at or after XT-083 emits complete criterion bindings and test-contract fields and cannot create a claimable placeholder.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-ADOPTION-002: agent prompts include the approved criteria, negative definitions, proof mode, focused gates, and allowed Red paths before code work starts.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-ADOPTION-003: relevant Delivery Plan, backlog, task-spec, manifest, workflow, or proof-runner changes make an active governed task stale and require a fresh checkpoint and review.
CRIT-FUTURE-TDD-ADOPTION-004: repository governance fixtures reject every documented bypass while all pre-XT-083 accepted and active records continue to validate unchanged.
Negative: compatibility code may read legacy records, but it must not let a new governed task omit TDD proof or criterion evidence.
Negative: no completed product task, historical handoff, or existing Delivery Plan is modified merely to manufacture past compliance.
